name: WorkflowMax reporting and migration utility
demand: There is a sizable platform around the problem, but no verified addressable-customer count: WorkflowMAX claims 100,000+ professionals across 150+ countries, without separating current paying users from legacy or historical users (https://workflowmax.com/about); Xero's UK site says 5 million customers worldwide, but does not disclose how many use WorkflowMAX (https://www.xero.com/uk/). Current review-directory signals include 123 WorkflowMax reviews on Capterra (page updated 29 Sep 2026) and 66 G2 reviews (G2 page analyzed May 2026); neither is an install or paid-user count (https://www.capterra.com/compare/120109-226306/Xero-vs-WorkflowMax, https://ai.g2.com/product/workflowmax). Xero App Store search results show 106 reviews, but that listing snapshot is stale and its most recent displayed review is 16 May 2025 (https://apps.xero.com/us/app/workflowmax-by-bluerock). Search volume, current installs, current paying accounts, and a relevant regulated-population count are unverified.
prices: WorkflowMAX's UK list price is £6.11/user/month Essentials (3-user minimum), £11.11 Pro (5-user minimum), and £18.89 Advanced (10-user minimum); annual prices shown are £5.50, £10, and £17 respectively. It already includes reporting, with AI-powered reporting on Advanced (https://workflowmax.com/pricing). Projectworks displays plans from $17/user/month, with a 10-user minimum, and standard onboarding including migration from $1,000; the currency shown by the retrieved pricing page is not identified, so currency is unverified (https://www.projectworks.com/pricing). Projectworks says its migration excludes WIP balances, documents, job templates, purchase orders, and reports, and asks customers to validate migrated data (https://help.projectworks.com/knowledge/migrating-from-bluerock-/-workflowmax). Adjacent, narrower Xero time-tracking alternative Hour Cap lists a free plan, Team at USD $10/month billed annually for two users, and Business at USD $30/month billed annually for four; it has no direct WorkflowMax importer, so it is not a migration or reporting replacement (https://hourcap.com/compare/hourcap-vs-workflowmax).
copy_speed: The incumbent is shipping quickly: WorkflowMAX lists Capacity Planning on 18 Apr 2026, an MCP connector on 14 Aug 2026, and a Harvest migration tool in its September 2026 release notes; it also offers custom reports, scheduled reports, and AI report insights (https://workflowmax.com/product-updates, https://support.workflowmax.com/hc/en-us/articles/25686306678553-Release-notes, https://support.workflowmax.com/hc/en-us/articles/54144993377945-About-scheduled-reports). Projectworks published a WorkflowMax-specific direct-extraction migration guide on 27 Jul 2026, including its mapping and validation steps; that is evidence of a live competing migration path, not proof that the path launched on that date (https://help.projectworks.com/knowledge/migrating-from-bluerock-/-workflowmax). I found no dated launch evidence for a new independent WorkflowMax data-quality validator since Apr 2026; that absence is unverified.
platform_risk: High. WorkflowMAX requires Pro or Advanced for API access and says API v1 will be switched off on 15 Jun 2027; a new product should use v2 (https://support.workflowmax.com/hc/en-us/articles/24773498748185-About-the-WorkflowMAX-API). Xero's current developer model charges by tier and API use: its FAQ lists Core at AUD $35/month and Plus at AUD $245/month, while Xero says App Store listing requires Plus or higher and certification (https://developer.xero.com/faq, https://developer.xero.com/documentation/xero-app-store/app-partner-guides/certification-checkpoints/). Xero's developer terms prohibit training or fine-tuning AI models on Xero API data and restrict passing that data to third parties without user consent (https://developer.xero.com/xero-developer-platform-terms-conditions). WorkflowMAX says customer data is hosted in AWS Sydney, relevant to handling UK customer data (https://workflowmax.com/faq).
defensible_asset: A plausible asset is a tested, versioned rules library that reconciles source and destination records, handles documented transformations such as split invoices, and produces an auditable exception report. Projectworks publishes specific mapping rules and omissions that give an initial testable ruleset (https://help.projectworks.com/knowledge/migrating-from-bluerock-/-workflowmax). This is a weak initial moat: the mapping is public, migration vendors can reproduce it, and customer data cannot safely become a reusable data asset by default; UK-specific proprietary data or meaningful switching costs are unverified (https://developer.xero.com/xero-developer-platform-terms-conditions).
build_effort: Start with a read-only CSV checker for one route, WorkflowMAX to Projectworks: compare clients, jobs, time entries, expenses, invoices, payment status, and WIP; flag the documented omissions and mapping differences. Projectworks itself lists checks for hours, billable rates, expenses, invoices, and WIP (https://help.projectworks.com/knowledge/migrating-from-bluerock-/-workflowmax). A secure, self-serve product would then need robust file parsing, reconciliation rules, deletion controls, and support for edge cases; direct WorkflowMAX API access is plan-gated, so API v2 can follow validation rather than precede it (https://support.workflowmax.com/hc/en-us/articles/24773498748185-About-the-WorkflowMAX-API). Exact production build time is unverified. Use deterministic checks for financial data; agents could assist with intake, report generation, routine support, and operations, subject to Xero's API-data restrictions.
channel: Use searchable, branded migration guides and a free sample checker, plus opt-in email and a Xero App Store listing only if the economics justify its tier and certification requirements (https://developer.xero.com/documentation/xero-app-store/app-partner-guides/certification-checkpoints/). Do not rely on cold messages: ICO guidance treats stored social-media DMs as electronic mail and requires consent for unsolicited electronic mail to sole traders and certain partnerships; corporate-subscriber email has different PECR rules but still has UK GDPR and opt-out duties where personal data is used (https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/, https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-direct-marketing-using-electronic-mail/key-concepts-for-direct-marketing-using-electronic-mail/).
owner_hours_per_week: unverified; <=5 hours/week is plausible only for a read-only, self-serve checker with limited asynchronous support. Bespoke migrations or manual exception handling could exceed the cap.
automation_share_pct: unverified; deterministic file checks and report delivery are automatable, but no operating product or measured workload exists yet to establish >=50%.
desk_test: Within one day, create a branded one-page offer and a sample reconciliation report using synthetic data, based on Projectworks' published migration mapping and omissions (https://help.projectworks.com/knowledge/migrating-from-bluerock-/-workflowmax). Publish it in relevant public channels where promotion is allowed and invite interested firms to opt in for a fixed-scope paid manual audit using a redacted export pair. Do not DM or cold-email prospects. Require a real company to provide a sample and commit to a paid pilot before building API integrations.
red_flags: The original trigger is weak: the Xero App Store complaint is dated 25 Mar 2025, over 18 months before 23 Oct 2026, and is self-reported, so it receives zero weight under the requested rule (https://apps.xero.com/us/app/workflowmax-by-bluerock). The claimed 12+ month release gap is contradicted by the official 2026 release notes (https://support.workflowmax.com/hc/en-us/articles/25686306678553-Release-notes). WorkflowMAX already has evolving reports, AI insights, and migration features, and Projectworks offers direct extraction plus migration validation; these reduce room for a broad reporting or migration replacement (https://workflowmax.com/pricing, https://help.projectworks.com/knowledge/migrating-from-bluerock-/-workflowmax). No independently verifiable revenue, paid-user count, current install count, or willingness-to-pay for this proposed utility was found. A migration checker may be a one-time purchase with support-heavy exceptions; both retention and <=5-hour weekly operation remain unproven.
